summary: A survey of how Christian churches responded to epidemics: Black Death processions, flagellants and anti-Jewish pogroms, a Spanish bishop who defied 1918 flu bans in Zamora, and churches spreading COVID-19 in 2020.

evidence.note: Black Death origins and arrival in Germany by 1349 open the historical survey
papally authorised mass processions spread plague; clergy death toll
long segment on flagellant bands and how they spread disease
Black Death pogroms against Jews, massacres in Strasbourg and Mainz
Clement VI issues bulls condemning blame of Jews for the plague
Bishop of Zamora introduced; Zamora segment is the longest single story
bishop defies gathering ban with novena and relic kissing in autumn 1918
US churches defying 1918 closures in Buffalo and Indianapolis
Shincheonji cluster in Daegu drives most South Korean COVID cases in 2020
US evangelical pastors defying COVID orders and calling bans persecution

notes: Survey episode with no single bastard; Catholic Church chosen as primary though US evangelicals and Shincheonji also feature. Bishop of Zamora's name rendered garbled in transcript; standard spelling used, lifespan from own knowledge. Transcript places Strasbourg in Germany; modern FR added. main_span equals covered_span because the survey has no narrower core.
